name: gp154_inversion_alpha_from_dimension
rubric_version_reason: v1.1 (2026-05-01): first run of the inversion substrate. The forward-regression direction was falsified earlier the same day; this rubric is the Newton-mode pivot to derive z = f(d_int) with PSLQ-recoverable constants. v1.1 adds spec-required persona / criteria / dimensions and aligns farther_tail_region to the null + custom-gate-harness convention.
description: Newton-mode substrate for the inversion principle: the scaling-law exponent z is hypothesized to be a closed-form function of the intrinsic dimensionality d of the data manifold. Anchor data is bahri2024 controlled image-classification rows where d is independently controlled. Pre-registered Kepler fit gives z = 0.62/d + 0.07. The Newton bar requires that at least one constant in the candidate closed form be PSLQ-recoverable as a named-constant ratio.
rubric_mode_reason: Discovery substrate. Open question: is the inversion principle's strict form correct, and what closed form has constants that are recoverable as ratios of named constants?
__do_not_run_live_reason: Dormant GP-154 fork with no matching project directory in the current repo; recover the project surface before running.
persona: You are an adversarial epistemic auditor for a closed-form scaling-law derivation. The substrate has 4 visible (z, d) pairs from a controlled experiment, plus a separately-held interpolation point (d=5.0) and a separately-held ambient-dimension extrapolation point (d=10^6). The discovery target is a closed-form z = f(d) with K_law <= 4 and at least one constant that is recoverable as a named-constant ratio (rational, multiple of pi/e/ln2/phi, etc.) within tolerance 1e-4. Reject any candidate that is just another curve fit. Reject Bahri-retrieval (a candidate that proposes z=4/d without earning it on this data). Reject any form that does not predict z -> 0 as d -> infinity. Reward derivations that come from approximation theory, information theory, fractal geometry, or harmonic analysis. The Kepler-fit baseline (z = 0.62/d + 0.07) is the lower bar to clear; the Newton bar requires PSLQ-recoverable constants and ambient-control passing. Be ruthless about the difference between a curve fit and a derivation.

dimensions.name: Closed-Form Discovery
dimensions.description: Find a compact closed-form z = f(d) with K_law <= 4. Full credit requires the form to predict z(d=5.0) within MAE 0.030 on holdout AND |z(d=10^6)| < 0.005 on the ambient-control extrapolation point.

dimensions.name: PSLQ Constant Recovery
dimensions.description: At least one fitted constant in the candidate closed form must be recoverable as a named-constant ratio within tolerance 1e-4. Library includes {1, 2, 3, 4, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/pi, 1/(2pi), 1/(2pi^2), 1/e, 1/ln(2), 1/phi, ln(2), 4/(2pi), e, pi, phi, sqrt(2)}. This is what separates a derivation from a curve fit; the Newton bar requires this gate to pass.

dimensions.name: Ambient-Control Limit
dimensions.description: The candidate must predict |z(d=10^6)| < 0.005, satisfying the strict inversion limit (z -> 0 as d -> infinity). Forms with non-vanishing additive bias terms (e.g., the Kepler fit's c0 = 0.07) fail this gate.

dimensions.name: Beat-Kepler Holdout
dimensions.description: The candidate must match or beat the Kepler-fit baseline (z = 0.62/d + 0.07) on holdout MAE within 10% tolerance. Pre-registered Kepler holdout MAE: 0.0067.

dimensions.name: Generative Yield (Variational / First-Principles)
dimensions.description: Required for Newton-mode rubrics per spec §18. The candidate primitive must name a distinct mathematically-orthogonal secondary observable beyond the primary z-prediction (e.g., a predicted ratio of α across two distinct d_int values, a predicted curvature d²α/dd², or a derived constant whose value is testable against a separate quantity). Full credit requires (a) a concrete variational/approximation-theoretic/information-theoretic derivation, AND (b) a pre-committed measurement method + expected value or range for the secondary observable. Partial credit (~50%) for naming a secondary observable without an evaluation method. Zero credit for restatements of z as the only prediction (Kepler-class naked fit).

dimensions.name: Rival Skepticism
dimensions.description: Compare against at least two rival forms, including (a) the Kepler-fit baseline z = 0.62/d + 0.07 and (b) Bahri's published prediction z = 4/d. Show why the proposed candidate beats both on the joint trio of holdout, ambient-control, and PSLQ gates.

criteria.Closed_Form_Discovery: Compact closed-form z = f(d) with K_law <= 4 that passes interpolation holdout (MAE < 0.030 at d=5.0) and ambient-control extrapolation (|z(d=10^6)| < 0.005).
criteria.PSLQ_Constant_Recovery: At least one fitted constant must match a named-constant ratio within tolerance 1e-4. Without this, the candidate is a curve fit, not a derivation.
criteria.Ambient_Control_Limit: Inversion principle requires z -> 0 as d -> infinity. Forms with additive bias that does not vanish at large d fail.
criteria.Beat_Kepler_Holdout: Match or beat Kepler-fit baseline (MAE 0.0067) on holdout within 10% tolerance.
criteria.Generative_Yield: Required for Newton mode (spec §18). Name a mathematically-orthogonal secondary observable beyond z-prediction; pre-commit to its measurement method and expected value/range. Bonus for variational/approximation-theoretic/information-theoretic derivation. Zero credit for z-only restatements.
criteria.Rival_Skepticism: Compare against Kepler baseline and Bahri's published z=4/d. Show the candidate beats both on the joint gate trio.

farther_tail_region_disable_reason: Custom gate_harness.py defines farther-tail as the variance-limited ambient-dimension row at d=1e6. The strict inversion principle requires |z| < 0.005 there.
disable_uniqueness_gap_gate_reason: Substrate is small (5 real-data rows + 1 ambient control). Rivals are judged by the joint trio: holdout MAE, ambient-control gate, and PSLQ constant recovery via custom gate_harness.py.
fit_primitive_features_k_max_reason: Pre-registered Kepler fit uses K=2 (slope c1, bias c0). Allow up to K=4 to admit forms like z = c1/d^p + c0 or z = c1/(d+d_floor). K>4 risks overfit on a 5-row substrate.
analogy_domain_hint: approximation theory and information theory; topological dimensionality; manifold geometry
enable_cold_llm_erdos_seed_reason: Cross-domain de-anchoring is critical here: the LLM mutator has read every neural-scaling-law paper. We must explicitly forbid the AI / deep-learning domain so the mutator derives structure from numbers, not from Bahri/Sharma-Kaplan retrieval.
cold_llm_seed_forbidden_domain: machine learning, deep learning, neural network scaling, AI, scaling laws, Bahri, Sharma-Kaplan, Kaplan, Chinchilla, intrinsic dimensionality of data manifolds, neural networks, transformers

cold_shot.prompt_extension: The substrate has 5 visible (z, d) pairs and 1 ambient-dim control (d=10^6, z near zero). The discovery target is a closed form z = f(d) with K_law <= 4 and at least one constant that is recoverable as a named-constant ratio (rational, multiple of pi/e/ln2/phi, etc.) within tolerance 1e-4. The empirical fit gives z ≈ 0.62/d + 0.07; your job is to either (a) propose a closed form that explains 0.62 and 0.07 as derived constants, or (b) propose a different functional form whose constants ARE derived. Cross-domain candidates from approximation theory, information theory, fractal geometry, and harmonic analysis are explicitly invited; do NOT cite specific neural-scaling-law papers. The candidate must satisfy z -> 0 as d -> infinity (no non-vanishing additive bias).

enable_lagrangian_derivation_reason: A variational / approximation-theory route is the path the inversion principle prescribes. The Lagrangian primitive should yield closed forms whose constants are PSLQ-recoverable.

evidence_contract.docstring: gp154_inversion_alpha_from_dimension is a Newton-mode substrate for the inversion principle. Each row is a (z, d, r, m) tuple where z is a fitted scaling exponent and d is the controlled intrinsic dimensionality of the data manifold.

killer_question: What closed form for z = f(d) has constants that are PSLQ-recoverable as named-constant ratios, while passing the ambient-control limit (z -> 0 as d -> infinity) and matching observed z within MAE 0.030 on the held-out d=5.0 point?
disable_evidence_fit_gate_reason: v3 multi-column substrate (z d q r m row_id) has categorical string columns that global_evidence_fit._parse_evidence rejects via float(); also I_model(features, params) API does not match the gate_s expected f(x) shape. The project_s own gate_harness.py runs evidence-row evaluation via the feature dict and is the correct evaluator.
enable_lagrangian_inversion_limit_guard_: v3 substrate has HARD STRUCTURAL CONSTRAINT 2 (inversion limit α(d→∞)→0); this rubric flag activates the apparatus-side Lagrangian-source-divergence guard so submissions with log_d / d^k / log(d) in J are rejected at R1 instead of silently failing the ambient gate.
